### 2.1 Amplitude Modulation & Sideband Analysis (Modulation)
- **Exam Weightage**: Tested in **61 PYQs** (Very High Yield)
- **Conceptual Summary**: Principles of amplitude modulation, carrier and sideband components $(f_c \pm f_m)$, modulation index, and power relationships.

#### Standard Mathematical Formulation
$$
\mu = \frac{A_m}{A_c} = \frac{A_{\text{max}} - A_{\text{min}}}{A_{\text{max}} + A_{\text{min}}}, \quad \text{Bandwidth} = 2f_m, \quad P_t = P_c\left(1 + \frac{\mu^2}{2}\right)
$$

#### Common Traps & JEE Pitfalls
> ⚠️ **Caution Point**: Modulation index $\mu$ must satisfy $\mu \le 1$ ($100\%$) to prevent envelope distortion.

#### Speed Hacks & Problem-Solving Tips
> 💡 **Speed Trick**: Carrier power does not depend on modulation index $\mu$, only sideband power increases as $\mu$ increases.

### 2.2 EM Wave Propagation & Space Communication (Wave Propagation)
- **Exam Weightage**: Tested in **37 PYQs** (Very High Yield)
- **Conceptual Summary**: Propagation modes of electromagnetic waves (ground, sky, and space waves), critical frequency, MUF, and antenna LOS range calculations.

#### Standard Mathematical Formulation
$$
d_{\text{max}} = \sqrt{2Rh_T} + \sqrt{2Rh_R}, \quad f_c = 9\sqrt{N_{\text{max}}}, \quad f_{\text{MUF}} = f_c \sec\theta_i, \quad \text{Antenna length } \ge \frac{\lambda}{4}
$$

#### Common Traps & JEE Pitfalls
> ⚠️ **Caution Point**: Ensure earth radius $R \approx 6400\,\text{km}$ and heights $h_T, h_R$ are converted into the exact same units before square rooting.

#### Speed Hacks & Problem-Solving Tips
> 💡 **Speed Trick**: For an antenna of height $h$, maximum range is $d = \sqrt{2Rh}$, and population covered is $\pi d^2 \times \rho$.

## Critical Exam Traps & Recurring JEE Mains Pitfalls in Communication Systems Out of syllabus

### 1. Sign Convention & Vector Inversion Errors
Paper-setters frequently exploit sign confusion in energy and potential differences. Always write the fundamental thermodynamic / vector definition before substituting numerical values.

### 2. Unit System Discrepancies
Molar conductivity (S cm^2 mol^-1 vs S m^2 mol^-1), SI vs CGS units, and micro/milli/nano multipliers (10^-3, 10^-6, 10^-9) account for over 35% of calculation mistakes in numerical type questions.

### 3. Boundary & Extreme Conditions
In transient circuits or limiting conditions (t=0+, t -> inf, infinite dilution, resonance), always check the asymptotic behavior of inductors, capacitors, and electrolyte mobility.

### 4. Direct Addition Fallacy
Never algebraically add intensive quantities (such as electrode potentials or AC component voltages) without accounting for electron weighting (n1*E1 + n2*E2 = n3*E3) or phasor vector geometry (V_total = sqrt(V_R^2 + (V_L - V_C)^2)).
